Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications. The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications. A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%). A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
articles.abstract: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies. In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; =0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups. Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target. Cost-effectiveness of recommended interventions for managing low back pain: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide. Although numerous treatment approaches are recommended by international clinical guidelines, there is still limited understanding of which interventions provide the best value for money. We aimed to critically appraise and summarise the evidence on the cost-effectiveness and costs of interventions endorsed in recent guidelines to manage low back pain (LBP), compared to usual care. We searched 10 electronic databases (e.g., MEDLINE (OvidSP), EMBASE (OvidSP), PsycINFO (OvidSP)) from inception to 9th of February 2026 for cost-effectiveness studies of guideline-recommended treatments to manage non-specific LBP. The primary outcome was cost/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), which was converted to 2024 Great British Pound values, tabulated and summarised qualitatively. Secondary outcomes were direct costs (total, interventional, health service use, community services and out-of-pocket costs) and indirect costs (e.g., lost wages, lost productivity, absenteeism). We assessed methodological quality using the Consensus Health Economics Criteria (CHEC) checklist for within-trial economic evaluations or the Philips checklist for modelling studies. Our review included 20 studies (17 within-trial economic evaluations and three modelling studies), published between 2005 and 2026. Half (n = 10) focussed on chronic LBP (>3-month duration), and eight included mixed populations (i.e., acute, subacute and chronic). All studies were of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions, both single-modality and multimodal interventions (e.g., exercise plus spinal manipulation; diet plus physical activity). Most interventions are cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000. Moreover, interventions aiming to reduce fear and stress or support self-management in people with chronic LBP, as well as clinician-delivered interventions including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support are potentially cost-saving from the healthcare, societal and payer's perspectives, as they are both more effective and less costly than usual care (e.g., first contact management, including advice and medication). All of the evidence is derived from high-income countries, and from a considerable heterogenous body of literature. Evidence on cost-effective treatments in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions that include education, psychological support, acupuncture and exercise seem to be cost-effective for managing LBP, compared to usual care. Improved access to and implementation of these effective treatments is urgently needed so more people can benefit from them in routine care. The review was registered on PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk; CRD42024510270).

articles.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy. Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

articles.title: Association Between Weight Loss on Incretin-Based Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
articles.abstract: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo. A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects. Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%). Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived glucose values versus venous plasma glucose values during oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) in youths with obesity, their effect on glycemic classification, and whether deconvolution-based reconstruction improves agreement. Twenty-nine youths with obesity underwent OGTT while wearing a FreeStyle Libre 2 sensor. Raw CGM values were temporally aligned with venous plasma glucose values and used to reconstruct plasma profiles via a first-order plasma-interstitial kinetic model and inverse filtering. Accuracy, agreement, consensus error grid, and glycemic classification were compared with collected venous plasma glucose values. Temporally aligned CGM-derived values showed limited agreement with collected venous plasma glucose values (mean absolute relative difference [MARD] 12.96%; 51.72% of values within ±10 mg/dL; 20.06% of values differing by >25 mg/dL) and caused classification shifts. After reconstruction, MARD decreased to 5.55%, the proportion of values within ±10 mg/dL increased to 75.86%, almost all values fell within consensus error grid zone A, and classification shifts were reduced. Deconvolution-based CGM reconstruction may support plasma-referenced, less invasive OGTT-based dysglycemic assessment.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of RCTs Using Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.
articles.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is a reasonable alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). We conducted an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC versus OAC in patients with AF. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/all-cause death. The primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. Secondary endpoints included net adverse clinical events, all-cause death, nonprocedure-related bleeding, and ischemic stroke. Reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis using a 2-stage approach and study-level meta-analysis using random-effects models were performed. Six trials enrolling 7,004 patients randomized to LAAC (n = 3,681) or OAC (n = 3,323) were included. There were no significant differences between LAAC versus OAC for the primary efficacy endpoint (difference in restricted mean survival time [∆RMST] -0.006 years, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.027 to 0.015 years, p = 0.56) or primary safety endpoint (∆RMST 0.004 years, 95% CI -0.025 to 0.034 years, p = 0.77) at 3 years. Nonprocedure-related bleeding was significantly lower with LAAC versus OAC (∆RMST 0.162 years, 95% CI 0.104 to 0.220 years, p <0.001) with no difference in all-cause death (∆RMST 0.029 years, 95% CI -0.031 to 0.089 years, p = 0.34). In a study-level meta-analysis, ischemic stroke was not significantly different with LAAC versus OAC (risk ratio 1.32, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.86, p = 0.09). In conclusion, the trade-off between a statistically significant lower risk of nonprocedure-related bleeding and a numerically, but not statistically, higher risk of ischemic stroke with LAAC versus OAC necessitates individualized risk assessment and shared decision-making for patients with AF at elevated risk of stroke.

articles.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
articles.abstract: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

articles.title: Fecal Immunochemical Test Outreach for Colorectal Cancer Screening in Community Health Centers: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening is suboptimal among people in traditionally underserved populations, many of whom receive primary care at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs). Mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) outreach improves screening, especially in underserved populations, but questions remain about impact over time. To evaluate the effectiveness of centralized annual mailed FIT outreach delivered over 3 years to increase CRC screening in FQHCs. articles.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting  messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. articles.title: Digital and Coaching Interventions for Uptake of Cancer Genetic Testing: The MiGHT Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Germline genetic testing (GT) for hereditary cancer risk can inform cancer treatment, screening, and prevention, yet testing rates remain low. Alternative strategies are needed to improve facilitation of GT. To compare 2 patient-level interventions to increase uptake of hereditary cancer GT against usual care. The Michigan Genetic Hereditary Testing (MiGHT) randomized clinical trial analyzed self-reported GT outcome data from participants meeting clinical GT criteria between April 21, 2022, and November 21, 2025. Participants were adults (age ≥18 years) who met national criteria for genetic evaluation and had not previously completed germline GT recruited from oncology, primary care, and gastroenterology practices; research registries; and the general public in Michigan. Data were analyzed from April 30, 2025, to May 1, 2026. Participants were randomized to either telephone-based health coaching, a self-directed digital intervention, or usual care. Both interventions incorporated genetics education and motivational interviewing concepts. GT uptake was assessed at 6- and 12-month time points. The primary outcome was completion of GT by 6 months. The effects of study group on GT uptake were evaluated using logistic regression, adjusting for cancer history, age, gender, and race. A total of 793 participants (median [IQR] age, 64 [51-71] years; 458 [57.8%] female) were randomized to health coaching (261 participants), the digital intervention (265 participants), or usual care (267 participants). Overall, 31 participants (4.9%) reported completing GT by the 6-month time point, and 76 participants (9.6%) underwent GT across the 12-month study period. Compared with usual care, participants in the digital intervention group had higher odds of completing GT by 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 3.88; 97.5% CI, 1.27-14.80), while those in the health coaching group had higher odds of completing GT by 12 months (AOR, 2.25; 97.5% CI, 1.11-4.77). Participants in the digital intervention group were more likely to express intention to test at 6 months (AOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.44-3.93), whereas those in the health coaching group had higher intention at both 6 (AOR, 2.99; 95% CI, 1.83-4.95) and 12 (AOR, 2.29; 95% CI 1.29-4.15) months compared with usual care. In this randomized clinical trial of GT interventions, GT uptake was higher among participants who received the digital or health coaching interventions compared with usual care, although overall testing rates were low. These results underscore the importance of content delivery, motivational messaging, and alternative GT care models. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05162846.

articles.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone. This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete. Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths. The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications. articles.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement. Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH. Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design. articles.title: Remote multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment in community settings: multisite randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common among community-dwelling older adults and represents a pragmatic target for community-level intervention. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a scalable, remotely delivered multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment, integrated into community and primary care settings. This 6-month, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial was performed at two public health centres in South Korea, enrolling adults aged 60-80 years with cognitive impairment and preserved functional independence. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to a videoconference-based exercise and nutritional support programme or to usual health promotion services. The primary outcome was change in the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Korean version (MoCA-K) score at 6 months; secondary outcomes included cognitive, functional, physical performance, frailty and depressive measures at 6 and 12 months. Among 140 participants (mean age 75.0 years; 60% female), equal numbers were randomised to intervention and control groups. At 6 months, the intervention group showed greater improvement in MoCA-K scores compared to the control group [2.3 points; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.4-3.1], and the difference was sustained at 12 months (1.1 points; 95% CI 0.3-2.0). The intervention was also associated with improvements in functional status and frailty at both time points. No intervention-related adverse events were reported. A remotely delivered multicomponent intervention improved cognition, functional independence and frailty in older adults with cognitive impairment identified through community-based screening. These findings support the effectiveness of scalable interventions integrated into community and primary care settings, particularly when access to in-person care is limited. articles.abstract: Given the high prevalence, chronicity, and associated disability of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), optimizing treatment is a global priority. articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). articles.title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
articles.abstract: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

articles.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography. TOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing. Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). Invasive interval cancers were detected within 12 months in 22 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (4·5 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 31 women in the digital mammography group (6·3 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; OR 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·97]). TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening. articles.title: Haemodiafiltration, haemofiltration and haemodialysis for adults with kidney failure.
articles.abstract: Convective extracorporeal dialysis modalities, haemofiltration (HF), haemodiafiltration (HDF), and acetate-free biofiltration (AFB), remove excess body fluid across the dialysis membrane through an interplay of positive and negative pressures and accumulated middle- and larger-sized solutes more efficiently than haemodialysis (HD). This increased removal of larger solutes, combined with the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid in convective dialysis, is hypothesised to reduce the frequency and severity of symptoms during HD and improve long-term clinical outcomes. This is an update of a review first published in 2006 and updated in 2015. To determine the benefits and harms of convective (HF, HDF, or AFB) versus diffusive (HD) dialysis modalities, or expanded HD (HDx), in preventing all-cause and cardiovascular death, cardiovascular morbidity, fatigue, and vascular access problems in adults with kidney failure. We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers up to 3 April 2025. Additionally, handsearching of journals and conference abstract books was performed, and the references of the included studies were reviewed. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing convective therapy (HF, HDF, AFB) with another convective therapy or with diffusive therapy (HD or HDx) for treating adults with kidney failure. Critical and important outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular death, nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, problems with vascular access, hospitalisation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Two authors independently assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool. We summarised treatment effects using the random-effects model and reported risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous data with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the confidence of the evidence using the GRADE approach. We identified 62 eligible studies (6897 participants). In total, 54 studies (6525 participants) compared HF, HDF or AFB with HD (both high-flux and low-flux); two studies (24 participants) compared AFB with HDF; three studies (62 participants) compared HDF with HF; and four studies (163 participants) compared HDx with HDF/HD. Convective dialysis, compared with diffusive therapy, likely reduces the risk of death (any cause) (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.96; I² = 0%; 15 studies, 5463 participantss; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92; I² = 0%; 9 studies, 4761 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Cardiovascular morbidity was likely not different between convective and diffusive dialysis (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.22; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 2074 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Little to no differences were found between convective and diffusive dialysis on fatigue (MD -0.95, 95% CI -2.50 to 0.60; 1 study, 543 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), problems with vascular access (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.50; 1 study, 124 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), hospitalisation (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 600 participants; low-certainty evidence due to indirectness and imprecision), or physical quality of life (MD 0.66, 95% CI -1.08 to 2.40; 1 study, 538 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision). Direct comparisons between different convective modalities were limited and underpowered to detect meaningful differences. Convective dialysis likely reduces all-cause and cardiovascular death. Effects on nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, vascular access failure, and hospitalisation are inconclusive. Future RCTs should prioritise methodological rigour and could focus on unresolved questions, including the impact of convective therapies on patient-centred outcomes such as symptom burden, HRQoL, functional status, and intradialytic tolerance, as well as investigating barriers to uptake, evaluating health system readiness, assessing cost-effectiveness, and identifying strategies to promote equitable access. articles.title: Half-dose rivaroxaban vs antiplatelet therapy for preventing silent cerebral embolism after left atrial appendage occlusion: the HALO-SCE trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal long-term antithrombotic strategy after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) remains undetermined. The present study aimed to investigate whether half-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) could better reduce silent cerebral embolic lesions (SCEs) and preserve cognitive function compared to antiplatelet therapy after successful LAAO. Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and cognitive assessments were repeated at 90, 180 and 365 days after LAAO. Secondary outcomes included cognitive trajectories, SCE burden, and a composite of all-cause mortality, clinical thromboembolic events and major bleeding. The composite clinical outcome occurred in 2.4% of the half-dose rivaroxaban group vs. 11.0% of the antiplatelet therapy group (P = 0.057). In patients eligible for oral anticoagulation after successful LAAO, rivaroxaban 10 mg daily significantly reduced SCEs and better maintained cognitive function compared with antiplatelet therapy, with numerically fewer composite clinical events.

articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain. To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock. Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026. Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter. The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics. There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]). articles.title: VERIFY: A Phase III Trial of Rusfertide Versus Placebo in Phlebotomy-Dependent Patients With Polycythemia Vera Receiving Standard-of-Care Therapy.
articles.abstract: Polycythemia vera (PV) is a myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by erythrocytosis. Rusfertide is a subcutaneous, injectable, hepcidin mimetic peptide that suppresses erythrocytosis. The phase III VERIFY trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of rusfertide in phlebotomy-dependent patients with PV and poorly controlled hematocrit. In VERIFY Part 1a (32 weeks), patients requiring frequent phlebotomy were randomly assigned (1:1, double-blind) to receive rusfertide or placebo with or without cytoreductive therapy. The primary efficacy end point was clinical response (absence of phlebotomy eligibility; weeks 20-32). Key secondary end points (baseline to week 32) included mean number of phlebotomies, proportion of patients who maintained hematocrit <45%, and mean change from baseline in patient-reported outcomes (Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System [PROMIS] Fatigue Short Form 8a [SF-8a] T score and Myelofibrosis Symptom Assessment Form [MFSAF] Total Symptom Score-7 items [TSS7]). Patients (N = 293) were randomly assigned to rusfertide (n = 147) or placebo (n = 146). Significantly more patients (n = 113, 77%) achieved a clinical response with rusfertide versus placebo (n = 48; 33%;  < .0001). Compared with placebo, rusfertide reduced mean ± standard deviation number of phlebotomies (0.5 ± 1.2  1.8 ± 1.5;  < .0001) and was superior in maintaining hematocrit <45% (n = 92 [63%]  n = 21 [14%];  < .0001). Rusfertide led to a significant improvement in the PROMIS Fatigue SF-8a T-score and MFSAF TSS7 versus placebo ( = .0252 and .0240, respectively). Injection site reactions, anemia, and fatigue were the most common adverse events. No deaths were reported. Rusfertide significantly improved hematocrit control, reduced the need for phlebotomy, and improved patient-reported symptoms versus placebo in phlebotomy-dependent patients with PV who were also receiving standard-of-care therapy.

articles.title: Effects of Blood Pressure Lowering by Hematoma Location in Acute Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: Early intensive blood pressure (BP) lowering is now recognized as an effective approach to improve outcome after acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). However, whether the effect varies by hematoma location is uncertain. We aimed to determine the heterogeneity of the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on functional outcome by hematoma location. We conducted a pooled analysis of individual patient-level data (IPD) from all 4 Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction in Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage Trials (INTERACT) and the second Antihypertensive Treatment of Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage (ATACH-II) trial, which were international, randomized, open, blinded end point assessed, controlled trials that investigated the effectiveness of early intensive BP control in acute ICH. ICH location was classified as lobar or deep hemisphere or infratentorial. The primary outcome was death or disability (modified Rankin Scale scores 3-6) at 90 days or 6 months (for INTERACT3). The heterogeneity of the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on the primary outcome by ICH location was estimated using generalized linear mixed models with trial as a random effect and adjustment for prespecified clinical covariates and an interaction term of "treatment-by-location." Among 11,288 patients (mean age 62.5 years [SD 12.7]; 4,056 [35.9%] women), 1,141 (10.1%) had lobar ICH, 9,202 (81.5%) had deep ICH and 945 (8.4%) had infratentorial ICH. Compared with deep or infratentorial ICH, lobar ICH occurred in older patients, was less often associated with intraventricular hemorrhage, and had larger hematoma volumes (all  < 0.001). The effect of intensive BP lowering on the primary outcome of death or disability differed by ICH location ( for interaction = 0.033). A clear benefit was only seen in deep ICH (adjusted odds ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.74-0.89;  < 0.001). Hematoma location modifies the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on functional outcome after ICH, with the benefit observed only in deep ICH. These trials are registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (INTERACT1 NCT00226096; INTERACT2 NCT00716079; INTERACT3 NCT03209258; INTERACT4 NCT03790800; and ATACH-II NCT01176565).

articles.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for Systemic Antibacterial and Antifungal Prophylaxis in Pediatric Patients With Cancer and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients: 2026 Update.
articles.abstract: To provide updated Pediatric Oncology Group of Ontario clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with cancer and hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) recipients. In this update, we harmonized procedures and recommendations across both the antibacterial and antifungal CPGs. Systematic reviews of randomized clinical trials evaluating systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric and adult patients with cancer and HCT recipients were updated. Using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, an international multidisciplinary panel revised or formulated recommendations and classified evidence quality. Good practice statements were also created. The updated search identified 13 new randomized trials published since 2019 (eight antibacterial and five antifungal), resulting in 195 total trials. The panel maintained a conditional recommendation to consider antibacterial prophylaxis in pediatric patients with AML and relapsed ALL and a strong recommendation to use levofloxacin when antibacterial prophylaxis is planned. A new conditional recommendation was introduced to consider using no antibacterial prophylaxis in patients unable to receive levofloxacin. Strong recommendations to use antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with AML and allogeneic HCT recipients and to use an echinocandin or a mold-active azole when antifungal prophylaxis is planned were maintained. Three new good practice statements were added, focusing on drug interactions, infection prevention practices, and monitoring infection epidemiology. This update consolidates and harmonizes CPGs for systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with cancer and HCT patients. Future research should refine prophylaxis indications for different patient subgroups.

articles.title: Insulin Dose-Adjusted Hemoglobin A1c Has Suboptimal Performance for Identifying C-Peptide-Defined Partial Remission: The SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth Study.
articles.abstract: Insulin dose-adjusted hemoglobin A1c (IDAA1c = HbA1c [%] + [4 × total daily dose in units/kg/day]) ≤9 is widely used to define partial remission in pediatric type 1 diabetes and as an eligibility criterion or outcome in disease-modifying therapy trials. However, it has not been validated in U.S. youth. Because higher BMI increases insulin resistance and insulin requirements, we hypothesized that IDAA1c would perform suboptimally in participants with overweight or obesity. We analyzed data from 422 SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth study participants with mixed-meal tolerance test (MMTT)-stimulated C-peptide within 12 months of diagnosis. Partial remission was defined using MMTT-stimulated area under the curve (AUC) mean C-peptide. Participant characteristics were compared by BMI category (<85th percentile [normal or underweight] and ≥85th percentile [overweight or obese]) using Wilcoxon rank sum and Fisher exact tests. Sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) AUC of IDAA1c ≤9 for identifying partial remission were evaluated. Participants with normal or underweight versus participants with overweight or obesity had lower IDAA1c (8.95 vs. 9.28, P = 0.043) despite lower stimulated C-peptide (1.25 vs. 1.88 ng/mL, P < 0.001). Overall, IDAA1c ≤9 had 61% sensitivity and 79% specificity for predicting C-peptide ≥0.91 ng/mL with an ROC AUC of 0.77. Among participants with overweight or obesity, sensitivity was 45% and specificity 81%. A Youden index-derived cutoff of IDAA1c ≤11.6 improved sensitivity to 93%, with specificity of 54% in participants with overweight or obesity. IDAA1c ≤9 demonstrated suboptimal accuracy as a screening test for partial remission, especially underestimating β-cell function in youth with overweight or obesity. BMI-specific cutoffs improved sensitivity but reduced specificity.

articles.title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025. Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone. The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention. Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone. Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine. articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Reduce Heart Failure Hospitalization, Cardiovascular Death and Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease are the principal drivers of morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in landmark trials, yet cross-trial inconsistencies in cardiovascular mortality, renal endpoints and drug-specific effects leave the class-level estimates incompletely synthesized. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 15 May 2026. Large placebo-controlled RCTs (≥ 1000 participants) and prespecified subgroup analyses in adults with T2DM were eligible. The primary outcome was the composite of first hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) or cardiovascular death (CV death). Secondary outcomes were 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), CV DEATH, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, first HHF and composite kidney outcomes. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects inverse-variance models. Fourteen studies (76 969 patients; 41 761 SGLT2i, 35 208 placebo) were included. SGLT2i reduced the primary composite by 23% (HR: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.73-0.81, p < 0.0001; I = 0%), with no effect modification by baseline HF (p-interaction = 0.82) or established ASCVD (p-interaction = 0.46). MACE was reduced by 14% (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92), driven by significant reductions in CV DEATH (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.93) and MI (HR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81-0.96), with no significant effect on stroke (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.81-1.08). First, HHF was reduced by 29% (HR: 0.71, 95% CI: 0.66-0.77) and composite kidney outcomes by 31% (HR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.60-0.79). SGLT2i confer consistent and clinically meaningful cardiorenal protection in T2DM across the full spectrum of cardiovascular and renal risk. The ertugliflozin estimate and the moderate heterogeneity in kidney outcomes should be interpreted in the context of trial-level clinical differences and nonstandardized kidney endpoint definitions. These findings support proactive, guideline-concordant initiation of evidence-based SGLT2i agents by endocrinologists, cardiologists and primary care providers as foundational therapy in T2DM.

articles.title: Petrelintide, a human amylin analogue for the treatment of obesity (ZUPREME 1): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract: Petrelintide is a novel, long-acting amylin analogue being developed for long-term treatment of obesity, leveraging a mechanism of action distinct from incretin-based treatments. This phase 2 trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly petrelintide versus placebo in people with obesity. This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involved 32 sites (public hospitals and private clinics) in Poland, Romania, and the USA. Adults aged at least 18 years without type 2 diabetes, with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m or with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m with hypertension or dyslipidaemia, or both, were randomly assigned (5:1) to self-administered subcutaneous injections of once-weekly maintenance doses of petrelintide (1·0-9·0 mg) or placebo for 42 weeks including dose escalation. Randomisation was done via a central interactive response technology system and was stratified by MRI participation. Participants, trial staff, and the study funder were masked to treatment assignment but not to different maintenance doses; masking was maintained by use of identical vials for petrelintide and placebo. The primary endpoint was percentage change in bodyweight from baseline after 28 weeks. Analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose. Missing data were assumed to be missing at random. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06662539) and the Clinical Trials Information System (2024-512549-18) and was completed on Mar 7, 2026. From Dec 9, 2024, to Feb 25, 2025, we screened 714 participants, of whom 493 were randomly assigned and 485 received at least one dose of petrelintide or placebo. 79 participants received at least one dose of treatment with petrelintide 1·0 mg, 81 with petrelintide 2·5 mg, 83 with petrelintide 5·0 mg, 79 with petrelintide 7·0 mg, 82 with petrelintide 9·0 mg, and 81 with placebo. 255 (53%) participants were female, 230 (47%) were male, mean age was 47 (SD 12) years, mean bodyweight 107·1 kg (20·3), mean BMI 36·7 kg/m (5·5), and 419 (86%) were White. Mean percentage change in bodyweight from baseline after 28 weeks (efficacy estimand) was -7·9% (95% CI -9·0 to -6·7) with petrelintide 1·0 mg, -7·9% (-9·0 to -6·7) with petrelintide 2·5 mg, -9·8% (-10·9 to -8·6) with petrelintide 5·0 mg, -9·3% (-10·5 to -8·2) with petrelintide 7·0 mg, and -9·4% (-10·5 to -8·3) with petrelintide 9·0 mg versus -1·7% (-2·8 to -0·5) with placebo. Estimated treatment differences versus placebo were -6·2% (-7·9 to -4·5) with petrelintide 1·0 mg, -6·2% (-7·8 to -4·5) with petrelintide 2·5 mg, -8·1% (-9·7 to -6·5) with petrelintide 5·0 mg, -7·7% (-9·3 to -6·0) with petrelintide 7·0 mg, and -7·7% (-9·4 to -6·1) with petrelintide 9·0 mg. Bodyweight continued to decline to week 42, with reductions of up to -10·7% with petrelintide. The most common adverse event with petrelintide was nausea (79 [20%] of 404 participants vs five [6%] participants with placebo). Vomiting was infrequent with petrelintide (12 [3%] participants vs five [6%] with placebo); active treatment and placebo had similarly low rates for diarrhoea (30 [7%] participants vs six [7%] with placebo) and constipation (28 [7%] vs three [4%] with placebo). No deaths were reported. Petrelintide achieved clinically meaningful weight reduction and had similar gastrointestinal tolerability to that of placebo apart from predominantly mild nausea during dose escalation, supporting further evaluation as a long-term obesity therapy. articles.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

articles.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.
articles.abstract: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges. We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point. A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2). Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.
articles.abstract: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH. We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete. Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]). Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH. Merck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

articles.title: Association Between Systemic Fluoroquinolones and Risk of Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone use has been associated with peripheral neuropathy in case reports, but there have been few noninterventional studies validating this association, and causality is unclear. The aim of this study was to estimate the association between systemic fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy relative to a comparator class of antibiotics, cephalosporins, using multiple databases to increase precision and assess the robustness of the results. Hazard ratios were similarly estimated for a positive control outcome of incident tendon rupture within 60 days of prescription. Risk differences for peripheral neuropathy were estimated using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator. Estimates were pooled across databases using fixed-effects meta-analysis. Potential residual confounding is a study limitation. Study results provide some reassurance to clinicians regarding risk of peripheral neuropathy with fluoroquinolones relative to a comparator antibiotic.

articles.title: The effects of an integrated nutrition-sensitive WASH, gender and poultry-value chain intervention on enteropathogen carriage in Burkinabe children: A secondary outcome analysis of the SELEVER cluster-randomized trial.
articles.abstract: We examined effects of a 3-year poultry- and livestock-focused Water, Sanitation and Hygiene intervention (WASH) on enteropathogen prevalence and density (SELEVER trial; ISRCTN16686478). Clusters of peri-urban and rural Burkinabe households were randomly assigned to: Control (no intervention), SELEVER (poultry rearing, nutrition, basic hygiene practices, and women empowerment) and SELEVER+WASH (additional intensive poultry- and livestock-focused community-led total sanitation). Base- and endline fecal samples were collected from children aged 24-59 months and analyzed using real-time qPCR to detect and quantify 24 enteropathogen targets. Analysis of effects on enteropathogen carriage and density was by intent to treat using logistic, log-linear and two-part regression. We enrolled 1,054 children and analyzed 883 children with endline fecal samples (attrition 15.0%). Almost all children (94.6%) were infected with at least one pathogen. Children in SELEVER+WASH arm had lower prevalence of Shigella/EIEC infection and unconditional mean DNA content compared to control (prevalence difference: -9.0%, 95% CI: -15.4%, -2.6%; unconditional DNA content: -56.5%, 95% CI: -78.8%, -11.1%) and SELEVER arms (prevalence difference: -7.7%, 95% CI: -14.2%, -1.3%; unconditional DNA content: -67.5%, 95% CI: -86.0%, -24.2%). Prevalence and unconditional DNA density of Hymenolepis nana was also lower in the SELEVER+WASH arm compared to control (prevalence difference: -4.9%, 95% CI: -9.4%, -0.5%; unconditional mean DNA content: -52.4%, 95% CI: -77.0%, -1.4%) and SELEVER (prevalence difference: -5.2%, 95% CI: -9.8%, -0.6%; unconditional mean DNA content: -52.7%, 95% CI: -79.0%, -0.7%). A poultry- and livestock-focused WASH intervention was associated with reductions in prevalence and density of Shigella/EIEC and Hymenolepis nana infections in young children in Burkina Faso.
